name: Airbus A319 (A319ceo)

reference.notes: CFM56-5B nacelle chosen because the AC lists the CFM56 as the primary ceo installation and CFM56 powers the largest share of ceo airframes (inferred, no in-service count found; V2500 is the alternative, AC intake x is 0.07 m further forward). Wingtip fence chosen because the AC presents it as the baseline ceo wing and Sharklets were only an option on ceo (new-build from late 2012, retrofit since 2013), so fences remain the most numerous ceo tip (inferred, unverified). Sharklet ceo variant: span 35.80 m, tip as the neo record. A319 plug: forward plug is 1.60 m shorter than A320 (main gear 11.04 m behind nose gear vs 12.64 m), aft 2.13 m shorter. Nacelle diameter 2.1 m is the width (fan-cowl section 2.07 m); the inlet lip section is 2.3 m tall because the lower lip droops. Nacelle length is lip to aft end of the reverser cowl (0.93+1.3+1.2 m); primary nozzle and centrebody add ~1.5 m more. Wing, fin and tailplane are identical across the family; only fuselage plugs move them (wing and engines shift with the forward plug, tail items follow the tail end). Fuselage station values are +-0.4 m (read from AC scale drawings).

name: Airbus A320neo

reference.notes: CFM LEAP-1A chosen over PW1100G: LEAP-1A has more orders (38.7% vs 28.5% of the A320neo family in Aircraft Commerce 2019, order share only; no current in-service split found) and is the AC's first-listed neo engine. PW1100G nacelle for comparison: 2.67 m wide, 3.65 m long (lip to reverser end), intake at the same x within 0.01 m; shorter and broader than the LEAP-1A. LEAP-1A nacelle 2.60 m wide (2.52 m tall incl. pylon fairing, so slightly oval), lip to aft end of reverser = 0.67+1.58+1.98 m = 4.23 m; primary nozzle and plug add ~1 m. Sharklets are standard on neo (AC shows only Sharklet), so this is the unique neo tip. Baseline plug length. The neo nacelle is visibly larger and longer than CFM56 (ceo is 2.1 m wide, 3.43 m long), sits higher relative to the wing, and the intake is 0.05 to 0.06 m further forward. Sharklet blade is nearly vertical (~7 deg from the front view) with a curved blend; the AC gives 1.61 m outward offset from wing tip (16.29 m semi-span) to the blade tip including the blend, and 2.43 m height. Wing, fin and tailplane are identical across the family; fuselage plugs shift wing/engines (forward plug) and the tail items (follow tail end). Fuselage station values are +-0.4 m. wingtip.rootY 16.29 m (AC p.45): the wing ends there and the sharklet leans the remaining 1.61 m outward, so dims.span stays the overall width.
